job_description:
Most Automatic Text Summarization implementations suck. They miss details and don't understand what is relevant and what isn't relevant, they miss facts and cannot distinguish the resolution a human can. Traditionally what we mean by a summary is a high-level overview that is "talking about" or "reporting on" what the content was. What I mean by summary is not this, but rather a "longer summary" recreation of the original content such that it is able to recreate the intention original material. This "longer" type of summary would be the equivalent of a human writing very complete notes.

The goal of the summarization I am describing is one of lossless compression: to recreate the experience of reading the book, article or listening to the transcript, podcast, seminar or meeting like you were there yourself in less time than it would take experience it all yourself. How do we distill the semantics down to less words without losing any details?

Types of input:

Books, Articles, Youtube Transcripts, Podcasts, Seminars/Events, Meeting Transcript

I suggest an approach that segments the task: break down the source material into clusters of meaning and working on each segment separately (but includes the entire context).

I see the path is a combination of Abstractive and Extractive summarization in such a way the summary "zooms out" when there is less relevance and "zooms in", sometimes quoting the text verbatim when it is more relevant (maybe semantic median of a vector cluster?).

This means, if the book was on advertising, what was the principles, ideas of the book, examples that demonstrate the principles, specific steps etc.

If the input was a youtube interview with Joe Rogan, who was the person being interviewed, what were their ideas, what was unique, what are the take aways?

If the input was a google ads expert giving a seminar about how to improve your clickthrough rate, what are the specific steps or sops shared (verbatim), what is the supporting evidence, explanation or metaphors for this approach and any unique tips ?

If the input was a meeting transcript, what was the topics discussed, points made, what requests were made (and therefore take aways for each participant), are the notes so complete that someone reading the notes and who didn't attend the meeting would know the same as someone who attended the meeting?

If the input was a philosphocial or self-help seminar, what was the questions given that had the listener go through a process about their own life and have a breakthrough? What were the relevant metaphors that had this happen?
